title: A Swarm Of UFOs Over Cheyenne?
excerpt: Most stories like this begin with the words "There I was." So does this one.
content:
A HERD OF UFOs OVER CHEYENNE, WYOMING?!

Well, no, and I'm sorry to disappoint.

Most stories like this begin with the words "There I was." So does this one.

There I was sitting in a little restaurant in Cheyenne, Wyoming. While eating, I was looking out the window when I saw those lights up in the sky.

But they weren't up in the sky. They were coming from - (insert dramatic music) - INSIDE THE RESTAURANT!

The ceiling lights inside were reflecting in the glass and looked like lights in the sky when looking through the window.

Look at that picture again, and you'll see what I mean. You'll see them as light fixtures. Since the window was double-paned glass, it looks like double the light images.

This leads me to the point I often make when someone reports seeing an alien spacecraft. Just because you don't know what it is does not mean it comes from outer space.

DARNIT! I was hoping for an alien invasion, like in the movie Independence Day.

The National UFO Reporting Center, yes, that is an actual website where you can report having seen a UFO, has recorded 421 total UFO reports in Wyoming.

Recently, Cowboy State Daily ran a story about a woman up in Gillette, Wyoming, who can't explain the strange lights she sees to her north in the night sky.

I'll admit, anyone would wonder what was going on if they saw those lights, orbiting and maybe even chasing each other, and not knowing what the heck it was.

I think I know.

Pilots look at maps that they call "sectional charts." That simply means that the maps were sectioned out for different parts of the USA and the world.

Some areas on these rather complicated maps show different-sized and shaped boxes blocking off large airspaces. Those areas are called MOAs.

A Military Operations Area (MOA) on an aeronautical chart is a designated block of airspace where the military conducts high-energy training activities—such as air combat maneuvers, aerobatics, formation flying, and low-altitude, high-speed tactics. (FAA).

Click on this link and look at the area in the northern part of Wyoming, southern Montana, and parts of North Dakota. You'll see those MOAs.

When military aircraft are practicing at night, they can light up the sky with their hot engines and even afterburners.

The lady in Gillette, Wyoming, is looking north into the night sky and seeing these lights dancing around. Anyone can understand why she is curious.

When fighter jets, for example, are practicing any number of maneuvers, even dogfighting, it would seem odd to anyone who did not know what they were looking at.

This is disappointing because I, too, want to be visited by aliens. But I don't want to be probed. Forget that.
